body: The fix should be similar to that for https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/pull/5070 by introducing `viewPath`.

I disaggre. My suggestion, we declare backend and frontend as module

``` php
'modules' => [
    'frontend' => [
        'basePath' => '@frontend',
        'controllerNamespace' => 'frontend\\controllers',
    ],
    'backend' => [
        'basePath' => '@backend',
        'controllerNamespace' => 'backend\\controllers',
    ],
],
```

As my suggestion, we use controllerID instead of controller className (like as gii/controller). When we want to generate crud for backend, we execute

```
./yii gii/crud --modelClass=common\\models\\User --controllerID=user --moduleID=backend
```
What if there are no modules, like in the advanced app?

Sory? If we have plan to generate crud for other application. They must declarated as module.
in console/config/main-local.php, i add 

``` php
return [
    'modules' => [
        'frontend' => [
            'class' => 'yii\\base\\Module',
            'basePath' => '@frontend',
            'controllerNamespace' => 'frontend\\controllers',
        ],
        'backend' => [
            'class' => 'yii\\base\\Module',
            'basePath' => '@backend',
            'controllerNamespace' => 'backend\\controllers',
        ],
    ],
];
```

(IMO You can add this at 'environments/dev/console/config/main-local.php'.)
then execute this

```
./yii gii/crud --modelClass=common\\models\\User --controllerClass=backend\\controllers\\UserController --moduleID=backend
```

its work, views generated at `@backend/views/user`. 

PS: last time i checked, we dont need to specify `class` for `modules`. But now its required (any discussion for this?).
Using `controllerClass` doesn't require you to declare the modules. The problem with controller ID is that it is interpreted differently in console and Web mode.

> Using controllerClass doesn't require you to declare the modules.

But it giving wrong in `viewPath`. `controllerClass` also not allowing generate controler with sub directory. 

> The problem with controller ID is that it is interpreted differently in console and Web mode.

Sory? what different? one generate `console\controllers` and other generate `backend\controllers`, is it?

i try this for gii/controller

```
./yii gii/controller --controller=backend/test
Running 'Controller Generator'...

The following files will be generated:
        [new] /home/mdmunir/NetBeansProjects/Yii2/yii2/apps/advanced/backend/controllers/TestController.php
        [new] /home/mdmunir/NetBeansProjects/Yii2/yii2/apps/advanced/backend/views/test/index.php

Ready to generate the selected files? (yes|no) [yes]:n
```

That's why I said the fix is to provide the `viewPath` option like in the `controller` generator.
It's unacceptable to require users to package an application in terms of a module.

In your example, you are specifying `controller` with a module ID prefix, and that's why it works fine. But if there's no module, you can't make it work. In fact, the latest code has changed `controller` to `controllerClass`.

```
./yii gii/crud --modelClass=common\\models\\User --controllerClass=backend\\controllers\\UserController --viewPath=@backend/views
```

vs

```
./yii gii/crud --modelClass=common\\models\\User --controllerClass=user --moduleID=backend
```

OK, you can close this issue. Actually, its not issue for me. I use my own generator. https://github.com/mdmsoft/yii2-gii/tree/master/generators/crud

I know using `controllerClass` is less pretty, but as I said we cannot require users to configure modules if their application simply doesn't have any modules. This issue is valid. So I will leave it open.
